method.c1Population: Complete pairs0,1,3 only;12 observations per arm per C1 route.
method.primaryHeadline: Pre-specified uninterrupted sensitivity, retaining original matched and unpaired observations separately.
method.fractions: Summary fractions are medians of each request union/HTTP, not ratios of medians. SQL spans and hold intervals overlap and are not additive.
method.pairDelta: For each pair0,1,3 and route, compute median HTTP and median union of the two optimized SQL hashes separately per arm. Delta=Bmedian-Amedian; summarize the3 deltas by nearest rank.
method.c4CategoryPopulation: ALL_OBSERVED B,32 requests per scenario, includes8 UNPAIRED B in two-tenant scenario; this section is descriptive costs, not A/B effects.
method.explain: Final PASS readiness8plans only. One EXPLAIN ANALYZE per arm/kind/revision; sum Actual Loops only over aclexplode Function Scan nodes. Root buffer totals avoid double counting inclusive plan nodes; missing JIT field is not a measured zero.

conclusion: B has lower latency in every observed matched HTTP pair and consistently lower metadata medians. Improvements remain in the pre-specified uninterrupted sensitivity. Metadata remains the dominant request cost; audit preparation contributes a visible concurrent tail. The interrupted campaign remains FAIL and does not establish a repaired timeout cause, capacity or production SLA.
limitations: Host not reserved; external workload/power conditions uncontrolled.
Node CPU is not PostgreSQL or host CPU; driver intervals include transport, execution and waits.
Sampled blockers lack request identity; sample counts are not blocked duration.
Authority lock acquisition includes its round trip; lock holds overlap SQL.
C4 audit-prepare tails alone do not identify which internal wait caused them.
No cache or checkpoint-removal recommendation follows from these measurements.
